newsitem.title: GERMANY: KLM eyes German shipper, forwarder forum.
newsitem.headline: KLM eyes German shipper, forwarder forum.

text.p: Air cargo shippers, forwarders and airlines in Germany should form a discussion forum to improve contacts and business relationships, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV said.
The airline's Frankfurt-based sales director Central & Eastern Europe, Oliver Evans, said a dialogue between the three players in the German industry was needed.
Speaking in a Reuters interview, he defended KLM's policy of doing business directly with large companies and stressed the airline was open to co-operation with freight forwarders.
Evans said: "We want to promote a healthy dialogue between the players in the industry. There needs to be a much more open platform where all three partners can talk about this."
"This is something I am seeking to promote and I would like others to join us," he added.
Despite boycott threats in the past from freight forwarders such as Schenker International, the airline had seen no effects on business in Germany, he claimed.
"Many forwarders have remained very loyal to KLM and we still want to work with forwarders. Some forwarders are more open to our ideas than others," Evans noted.
"We have no secret of the fact we are meeting with shippers as do a number of competitiors. This will continue in the future," he added.

"We very much wish to keep in touch with the major shippers in the market. We need to have a direct relationship with these major users of airfreight as we are essentially providing a customised service."

It was up to shippers to decide whether the forwarder would be involved in sales talks between the company and KLM but since forwarders offered services which KLM could not, they remained involved, he pointed out.
"Forwarders understand our position, support it and in many cases they started the contacts with shippers which we have," he noted.
For example, agents often asked KLM to pick up cargo directly from shippers since this was often cheaper than using their own staff. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
